Empirical Research Plan –  “Are Teacher Value-Added Forecasts Biased by Non-Random Student Sorting?”

------------------------------------------------------------------------------

1. Identification Strategy
------------------------------------------------------------------
Primary strategy:  Difference-in-Differences / Event-Study that exploits year-to-year changes in the set of teachers who teach the same school-grade-subject (SGS) cell.

Rationale  
•  The key source of plausibly exogenous variation is teacher turnover and grade-switching. When a high- (or low-) value-added (VA) teacher enters or exits a SGS cell, the average predicted teacher quality facing the next cohort changes discretely, while the principal, curriculum, building resources, and peer composition are largely fixed.  
•  Comparing adjacent cohorts in the same SGS cell therefore “differences out” any time-invariant, grade-invariant, or school-invariant determinants of achievement, and sharply attenuates within-year sorting concerns.  
•  An event-study around the entry/exit provides a visual pre-trend test of the DID parallel-trends assumption.

Notation  
i  = student, s = school, g = grade, j = teacher, c = cohort (year t), k = subject.  
Yisgjkt  = end-of-year standardized test score (mean 0, sd 1 in the district × grade × year).  
VÂjt     = leave-year-out estimate of teacher j’s value-added in year t (in student-level SD units).  
TREATsgkt = average (student-weighted) VÂ of all teachers who teach grade g, school s, subject k in year t that a student is exposed to.

Estimating equation (DID):  
Yisgjkt = β · TREATsgkt + λsgk + τt + ψXit + εisgjkt    (1)

λsgk = SGS fixed effects remove permanent differences; τt = district-wide year shocks (accounting for trends in curricula, accountability pressure, etc.).  
Xit = lagged test score, ethnicity, gender, special-ed, and parental log-income.  
β measures how one SD higher predicted teacher quality for a cohort translates into student achievement for that cohort. If teacher VA forecasts are unbiased, β ≈ 1.

Event-Study specification: Create an “event time” variable E = (year – year of high-VA entry/exit) and estimate:

ȲsgkE = Σℓ≠−1 θℓ · 1{E=ℓ} + λsgk + τt + υsgkE           (2)

Omitting ℓ = –1 (the year before the event) gives a dynamic treatment effect trace; flat pre-period coefficients provide a direct check for selection on trends.

2. Treatment and Control
------------------------------------------------------------------
Treatment variable  
TREATsgkt = mean of leave-year-out predicted VÂjt for the set of teachers assigned to cohort t in school s, grade g, subject k. A one-unit increase equals a one standard-deviation predicted improvement in teachers.

Control group  
The implicit control is cohorts in the same SGS cell in other years that experienced smaller (or opposite-signed) changes in predicted teacher quality.

Treatment timing / event date  
Year t in which the composition of teachers in a SGS cell first changes because (i) a teacher with VÂ in the top (or bottom) decile enters, (ii) a top/bottom-decile teacher exits, or (iii) a mid-VA teacher is replaced by a substantially higher- or lower-VA teacher (|ΔVÂ| ≥ 0.5 SD).

3. Key Identifying Assumptions
------------------------------------------------------------------
A1. Parallel Trends / Cohort Comparability  
Absent teacher-composition shocks, adjacent cohorts in the same SGS cell would have followed parallel achievement paths.

Plausibility: Same principal, curriculum, facilities, and neighborhood catchment; district has little ability or incentive to differentially time curricular changes exactly when a particular teacher moves.

A2. Exogenous Teacher Mobility Relative to Unobserved Student Ability  
Teacher entry/exit or grade-switching is not systematically driven by time-varying unobservable student characteristics within that SGS cell.

Plausibility: Grade assignments often determined by teacher preference, seniority, or staffing constraints rather than fine-grained forecasts of next year’s incoming cohort ability (which principals observe only after staffing is set). We will test by looking for pre-treatment trends (event study) and by showing balance in lagged scores and SES across cohorts with large vs. small VÂ shocks.

A3. No General-Equilibrium or Spillover Effects Across Grades / Subjects  
A change in the grade-g math teaching staff does not itself alter grade-g English achievement (except through common teacher assignments) or the unobserved determinants of neighboring grades.

Plausibility: Separate teachers by subject in middle school and normally distinct cohorts per grade. We will include subject×year FE and verify no cross-subject impacts.

4. Threats to Identification and Mitigation
------------------------------------------------------------------
Threat 1 – Time-varying shocks correlated with teacher turnover (e.g., new curriculum, coach arrival)  
Response:  Add SGS×subject×linear-time trends; control for cohort mean lagged test score; include staff FTE counts, class size, and per-pupil expenditure if available. Run placebo on neighboring grades that did not experience turnover.

Threat 2 – Non-random student mobility across years (families may transfer because a “star” teacher is rumored to arrive)  
Response:  Show that entering and exiting student counts, parental income, and prior scores do not jump in the event year. Estimate models with and without movers; re-weight by inverse probability of staying.

Threat 3 – Mechanical attenuation from measurement error in VÂjt (classical error biases β toward zero)  
Response:  Use Empirical Bayes shrinkage VÂ estimates (already produced) to minimize noise, and instrument TREATsgkt with an indicator for the entry/exit of a top-decile teacher (first-stage F>10). IV corrects for attenuation.

5. R Code Outline
------------------------------------------------------------------
```r
########################################
# 0. Packages
########################################
library(data.table)   # fast data wrangling
library(fixest)       # high-dimensional FE
library(ivreg)        # 2SLS robustness
library(ggplot2)

########################################
# 1. Load data
########################################
stu <- fread("student_level_panel.csv")    # unit: student-subject-year
teach <- fread("teacher_va_estimates.csv") # teacher-year VÂ

########################################
# 2. Merge and construct variables
########################################
stu <- merge(stu, teach[, .(teacher_id, year, subject, VA_hat = VA_leaveout)],
             by = c("teacher_id", "year", "subject"), all.x = TRUE)

# Cohort-level weighted mean of predicted VÂ
cohort_va <- stu[, .(TREAT = weighted.mean(VA_hat, w = 1),  # equal weight
                      Ybar  = mean(test_score_std),
                      LagY  = mean(lag_test_score_std)),
                 by = .(school_id, grade, subject, year)]
setkey(cohort_va, school_id, grade, subject, year)
stu <- merge(stu, cohort_va[, .(school_id, grade, subject, year, TREAT)],
             by = c("school_id", "grade", "subject", "year"))

########################################
# 3. Main DID regression
########################################
did_mod <- feols(test_score_std ~ TREAT + lag_test_score_std +
                  gender + ethnicity + special_ed + log_parent_income |
                  school_id^grade^subject + year,
                  data = stu,  cluster = ~school_id^grade^subject)

summary(did_mod)

########################################
# 4. Event-study (cohort level)
########################################
# Identify entry/exit of top-decile teachers
teach[, highVA := as.integer(VA_hat >= quantile(VA_hat, .9)), by = subject]
moves <- teach[highVA == 1, 
               .(entry_year = min(year), exit_year = max(year)),
               by = .(teacher_id, school_id, grade, subject)]

# Construct event time E
cohort_va <- merge(cohort_va, moves, by = c("school_id","grade","subject"), all.x = TRUE)
cohort_va[, E := year - entry_year]        # analogous for exit; keep the closer one
cohort_va <- cohort_va[!is.na(E) & abs(E) <= 5]  # ±5-year window

es_mod <- feols(Ybar ~ i(E, ref = -1) + LagY |
                school_id^grade^subject + year,
                data = cohort_va, weights = NULL, cluster = ~school_id^grade^subject)
iplot(es_mod)   # ggplot of θℓ coefficients

########################################
# 5. IV robustness: instrument TREAT with
#    indicator for top-decile teacher entry
########################################
cohort_va[, Z := as.integer(E == 0)]        # treat entry year as instrument
iv_mod <- ivreg(test_score_std ~ TREAT + lag_test_score_std + gender +
                ethnicity + special_ed + log_parent_income |
                Z + lag_test_score_std + gender + ethnicity +
                special_ed + log_parent_income,
                data = stu)
summary(iv_mod, diagnostics = TRUE)
```

6. Expected Results
------------------------------------------------------------------
Economic priors suggest that one SD increase in teacher quality (as measured by forecasted VA) should translate into roughly one-for-one increases in realized student gains (β ≈ 0.9 – 1.1). If non-random sorting upwardly biases VÂ, β will fall short of 1; if high-ability students systematically cluster in classes of high-VA teachers, β < 1 after we remove controls. My prior is that district sorting is moderate; I expect β ≈ 0.95 with a 95 % CI of [0.85, 1.05].

7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (DID)
------------------------------------------------------------------
C1: No differential pre-trends (visual event-study) ……… 1  
C2: Exogeneity of teacher mobility to unobservables …… 0.5  
C3: Stable composition of SGS cells (no selective mobility) … 0.5  
C4: No interference/spillovers across units ………………… 1  
C5: Correct standard-error clustering and weighting …… 1  

Overall: 4/5. Remaining concerns center on whether teacher moves are partly anticipatory (C2) and whether families systematically sort (C3). Both are testable and will be probed as outlined above.
